Definition: from G4862 and βιβάζω (to force; causative (by reduplication) of the base of G939); to drive together, i.e. unite (in association or affection), (mentally) to infer, show, teach:--compact, assuredly gather, intrust, knit together, prove.
BiblicalUsage: Paul prays that the Colossians' hearts would be knit together in love, and Luke says Saul confounded the Jews at Damascus by proving that Jesus is the Christ. The word joins hearts together and fits proof together, and both are the work of the Spirit: love that holds people fast and truth that holds together under testing.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that love and proof belong together, and I hold that a church knit together in love is the best argument that Jesus is the Christ.
